own_solution.law: SI unit conversion: 1 kJ = 1000 J, 1 mJ = 1e-3 J, 1 N*m = 1 J
assumptions: N*m here denotes work/energy (N times m), not torque

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: Three renderings (1000 J, 1000000 mJ, 1000 N*m) all equal 1000 J, but the second rendering states 1.1 kJ = 1100 J, so it is not an equivalent rendering of the same quantity and the answer is not invariant across renderings.

counterexamples: Rendering 2: 1.1 kJ converts to 1100 J, not 1000 J, so a model answering 1000 J for every rendering would be wrong on rendering 2, and a correct 1100 J would be scored wrong if the certified answer is a single 1000 J.
notes: Per-rendering answers: 1000 J, 1100 J, 1000 J, 1000 J. If the item intends a unit-rendering invariance test (same energy written in different units), rendering 2 breaks it (should be 1 kJ or 1.0 kJ). If instead rendering 2 is intended to be a different value, the item is not a set of renderings of one problem. Either way the set is inconsistent. Each individual question is trivially well-posed. Writing N*m for energy is dimensionally fine but is conventionally reserved for torque; minor. The phrase 'energy change is stated as ... What is that energy in joules?' is an artificial pure unit-conversion task.
